UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                 BEFORE THE
                   FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION




Southern Indiana Gas and Electric            )
Company                                      )
                                             )
v.                                           )              Docket No. EL26-38-000
                                             )
Midcontinent Independent System              )
      Operator, Inc.                         )


              LIMITED COMMENTS OF THE SOUTHERN REGULATORS

       Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC”

or “Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212 and 385.214, and the

Combined Notice #3 issued on January 6, 2026, the Arkansas Public Service Commission and the

Council of the City of New Orleans (collectively "Southern Regulators"), 1 submit these limited

comments to the Southern Indiana Gas and Electric Company’s (“SIGECO”) “Complaint

Requesting Fast Track Processing,” filed on January 5, 2026. 2

       As detailed below, the instant Complaint is fact specific.       Therefore, the Southern

Regulators request that any Commission findings or directives in this proceeding also be limited

to the facts in the Complaint.




1
       Each of the Southern Regulators have filed their own doc-less interventions in this docket,
       and therefore, are already parties to this proceeding.
2
       See S. Ind. Gas and Elec. Co. v. Midcontinent Indep. Sys. Operator, Inc., Docket No.
       EL26-38-000 (Jan. 5, 2026) (“Complaint”).


                                                 -1-
 I.     BACKGROUND

       F.B. Culley Generating Station is an electric generating facility located in Warrick County,

Indiana. The Culley facility is owned and operated by SIGECO (subsidiary of CenterPoint Energy,

Inc.) and consists of two coal-fired generation units, Unit 2 (103.7 MW) and Unit 3 (265.2 MW),

with a combined nameplate capacity of approximately 368.9 MW. 3 Unit 2 and Unit 3 began

commercial operations in 1966 and 1973, respectively. Unit 2 has been scheduled to cease

operations on December 31, 2025, consistent with SIGECO’s commitments in the Indiana Utility

Regulatory Commission approved settlement agreements in Cause No. 45990 (February 3, 2025,

as modified Marcy 19, 2025).4

       On December 23, 2025, the U.S. Secretary of Energy issued an order pursuant to Federal

Power Act (“FPA”) section 202(c) and section 301(b) of the Department of Energy Organization

Act5 declaring that “an emergency exists in portions of the Midwest region of the United States

due to a shortage of electric energy, a shortage of facilities for the generation of electric energy,

and other causes.”6 Accordingly, the DOE Order directed that both CenterPoint and Midcontinent

Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) “take all measures necessary to ensure” that Culley

Unit 2 is available to operate until March 23, 2026.7




3

4

       offer into the MISO market and to produce energy when dispatched. Id. at 2 and n.15.

6

7

                                                -2-
        In complying with the DOE Order, SIGECO is incurring and will continue to incur costs

as it makes Culley Unit 2 available into the MISO market and produces energy when dispatched. 8

However, MISO’s existing Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets

Tariff (“Tariff”) does not include a mechanism for SIGECO to recover costs associated with

complying with the DOE Order.9 In addition, MISO lacks Tariff authority to unilaterally offer

SIGECO a FPA section 202(c) rate agreement.10

       The DOE Order stated that “[r]ate recovery is available pursuant to [FPA section 202(c)],”

and further directed CenterPoint to “file with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Tariff

revisions or waivers necessary to effectuate this order.” 11 SIGECO states that it intends to

separately file the actual costs associated with running Culley Unit 2 from the date of the DOE

Order, netting out applicable market revenues, i.e., its “Order Costs”.12 But, here, SIGECO files

the instant Complaint requesting that the Commission exercise its authority pursuant to FPA

sections 202(c) and 309, or in the alternative section 206, to order MISO to adopt a Tariff revision

for SIGECO to recover the Order Costs from complying with the DOE Order. 13 SIGECO requests

that the requested MISO Tariff revision be effective as of the issuance of the DOE Order on

December 23, 2025, or such other date as the Commission finds appropriate to allow SIGECO to

recover costs associated with the DOE 202(c) Order. 14

                                               -3-
 II.    LIMITED COMMENTS

       Since 2020, the Department of Energy (“DOE”) has exercised its authority under Section

202(c) primarily in response to extreme weather conditions.15 In contrast, here the DOE has

declared emergency conditions exists under more generalized reliability concerns due to

“increasing demand and shortage from accelerated retirement of generation facilities…in the near

term and … likely to continue in subsequent years” 16 As a result, the DOE has taken the

extraordinary step of delaying Culley Unit 2’s planned retirement, requiring CenterPoint to ensure

Cully Unit 2 is available to operate, and directing MISO to economically dispatch Culley Unit 2

“to minimize cost to ratepayers.” 17

       Due to the unique circumstances underlying the DOE Order and the relief requested under

the Complaint, the Southern Regulators submit these limited comments to ensure that the

Commission’s actions are confined to the specific facts presented in the Complaint.

       A.      SIGECO’s Proposed Rate Recovery Mechanism is Applicable Only to Culley
               Unit 2.

       In the Complaint, SIGECO’s only request for relief is for the Commission to direct MISO

to revise its Tariff to include a mechanism to effectuate SIGECO’s cost recovery of the Order Costs

incurred due to the DOE Order.18 Specifically, Attachment A of the Complaint includes a proposed

       See U.S. Dept. of Energy, DOE’s Use of Federal Power Act Emergency Authority,
       available  at    https://www.energy.gov/ceser/does-use-federal-power-act-emergency-
       authority.
16
       See DOE Order at 5.
17

18

                                               -4-
 schedule for MISO’s Tariff entitled “Allocation of Costs Associated with Continued Availability

of Unit 2 of F.B. Culley Generation Station Pursuant to DOE Order No. 202-25-13.” 19

       The Southern Regulators do not take a position on either SIGECO’s requested relief, the

Commission’s authority to grant the requested relief, or whether SIGECO’s proposed schedule is

just and reasonable. Rather, the Southern Regulators draw attention to the fact that both the DOE

Order and the proposed schedule contain explicit language that the cost recovery mechanism is

related only to the facts underlying the DOE Order and Culley Unit 2. In other words, any rate

recovery schedule that the Commission may accept in this proceeding will not be of general

applicability under MISO’s Tariff but will be limited to SIGECO’s Culley Unit 2 and the Order

Costs incurred due to the DOE Order. The Southern Regulators request that this point is made

clear in any Commission order in this case.

       B.     As proposed, the Order Costs for Culley Unit 2 Are Not (and Should Not Be)
              Allocated to the MISO South Subregion.

       In addition to proposing a cost recovery mechanism for the Order Costs, the Complaint

also asks the Commission to adopt the cost allocation in its proposed schedule in Attachment A to

the Complaint.20 Specifically, SIGECO proposes to allocate the Order Costs to MISO’s north and

central zones (i.e., Zones 1-7) on a load ratio share basis.21 In support, SIGECO argues that the

DOE Order identified the reliability risks in those MISO zones as the basis for declaring the

emergency and requiring the continued operation of Culley Unit 2. 22 Therefore, consistent with

                                              -5-
 general beneficiary pays and cost causation principles, SIGECO argues the Commission should

find its proposed cost allocation in Attachment A is just and reasonable. 23

       Again, the Southern Regulators do not take a position on either SIGECO’s proposed cost

allocation to MISO Zones 1-7, the Commission’s authority to grant the requested cost allocation,

or whether SIGECO demonstrated that such allocation is either appropriate or justified under cost

causation or beneficiary pays principles. But, the Southern Regulators agree that none of the Order

Costs should be allocated to the MISO South subregion. In doing so, the Southern Regulators do

not endorse the proposed scope of the cost allocation as defined by the DOE Order. Moreover,

due to the fact-specific Complaint, the Southern Regulators urge the Commission to make clear

that any finding or directive on cost allocation in this proceeding does not set any precedent for

future orders, pursuant to section 202(c).




23

                                                -6-
 III.   CONCLUSION

       For the reasons stated above, the Southern Regulators respectfully request that the

Commission accept the limited comments submitted herein in conjunction with its determinations

on the Complaint in the instant proceeding.
